questions.q: What does Finance's page lead with, in contrast to Support's page?
options: A dollar total first, trend second — the opposite emphasis from Support's page
A trend chart first, with no headline number at all
A raw table of every refund event with no aggregation
A list of subscriber names sorted alphabetically
questions.explain: Finance's real question is 'how much, right now' — so the page leads with a headline total, unlike Support's trend-first design.

questions.q: Why does this lesson put refund_event_count visibly on the page, not just leave it in the underlying view?
options: So anyone looking at the page, not just someone digging in Snowflake, has a chance of noticing if the count looks structurally wrong
Power BI requires every card visual to have a matching count visual
It's purely decorative and has no diagnostic purpose
refund_event_count cannot be queried directly from Snowflake, only displayed in Power BI
questions.explain: Surfacing the sanity-check column on the page itself makes a structural problem noticeable without requiring anyone to dig into the SQL.

questions.q: What does total_refund_amount's currency formatting use?
options: Power BI's column formatting, since the value already arrives as a clean NUMBER(10,2) from the view
A custom DAX FORMAT() measure
A Snowflake stored procedure that reformats the column before export
Manual text entry for each value
questions.explain: Since the view already returns a clean numeric type, ordinary Power BI column formatting is sufficient — no DAX needed.

questions.q: What does the subscriber slicer on this page let Finance do?
options: Drill into one subscriber's refund history specifically, useful for investigating an individual account
Change which Snowflake warehouse the report queries
Switch between Import and DirectQuery mode
Filter which Power BI file is currently open
questions.explain: The subscriber slicer supports investigating an individual account's refund history, beyond the weekly aggregate view.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say a correctly-built Finance page still can't protect Finance from a wrong number?
options: A report page accurately reflects whatever is in refund_events at refresh time — if the underlying data is wrong, the page will correctly display the wrong number
Power BI pages are inherently unreliable regardless of how they're built
Finance's page was deliberately built incorrectly in this lesson
It's not true — a correctly-built page guarantees correct numbers in all cases
questions.explain: A report page's correctness is about accurately reflecting its source — it can't catch a problem upstream in the pipeline feeding it, which is exactly where Lesson 13's bug lives.
